newsitem.title: UK: Phillips declares force majeure at Ekofisk terminal.
newsitem.headline: Phillips declares force majeure at Ekofisk terminal.

text.p: Phillips Petroleum said on Wednesday it was declaring force majeure on Ekofisk crude oil loadings at its Seal Sands terminal, traders said.

In a telex sent on Wednesday to customers, Phillips, which operates the Norwegian Ekofisk oilfield, said "during this time" it was declaring force majeure at Britain's Seal Sands terminal, to which the crude is piped, because of the temporary shutdown of production.
Traders receiving the telex said it did not say how many cargoes would be affected by the force majeure or if any would be cancelled.
On Wednesday, a Phillips' spokesman said his company hoped to retart the 350,000-barrel-per-day field on Thursday once repairs to stop a small gas leak on the pipeline were completed.

Output at the field was halted early on Tuesday. The spokesman said oil from third party fields -- British Petroleum's Gyda and Ula and Amoco's Valhall and Hod -- and the Statpipe gas line continued to flow.
